text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Security forces kill "terrorist" in the northeastern province of Tizi-Ouzou.
- Sugar shortage in the domestic market prompts trade ministry to review trade regulations to ensure better supply of foodstuffs.
- Hospital doctors, who staged a strike to back demands for more pay, hold talks with health ministry officials. Union officials to meet on Monday to assess the talks.
- More than 2,000 managers of state enterprises are suspected of criminal offences, including questionable deals harming their companies' interests.
- Main workers union policy-making body convenes to discuss taking part in constitutional reform referendum and outcome of their talks with government over minimum wage increase.

- Islamist Nahda, Movement for Democracy in Algeria and Socialist Forces Front parties discuss possible coordination between the three parties in next elections. Anti-Islamist Rally for Culture and Democracy seeks to unite pro-democracy political forces.
